summary: SeleneSight is an interactive 3D web application that enables mission planners, researchers, and students to evaluate and compare potential landing sites across the lunar south pole. By combining high-resolution topography from NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) with JPL solar and terrestrial ephemeris data, our platform calculates real-time Sun elevation angles and direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight communication windows for any selected coordinate and mission date. Planning lunar south pole missions is uniquely challenging due to extreme terrain, permanently shadowed craters, and narrow solar power windows. SeleneSight bridges the gap between raw astrodynamics datasets and rapid decision-making through clear, accessible visualizations of power generation potential, terrain slope hazards, and communication availability.
details:
SeleneSight provides an interactive digital twin of the lunar south pole where users can select candidate landing coordinates, scrub through mission timelines, and immediately compare site viability based on solar illumination, terrain slope, and Earth visibility.

​How It Works:

​1. Terrain & Horizon Modeling: Using elevation models from NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), the system reconstructs local topographic horizons around any chosen landing site to account for crater rims and steep ridges that block sunlight or radio signals.2. Ephemeris & Line-of-Sight Calculation: Integrating NASA JPL Horizons ephemeris data, the engine computes Sun elevation angles (to estimate solar array power generation) and Earth elevation/azimuth angles (accounting for lunar libration) to determine uninterrupted Direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows.

​3. Comparative Site Scoring: Users can compare multiple landing sites side-by-side across customizable mission durations, exporting high-clarity visibility charts and terrain hazard summaries

Benefits & Impact:

​Agile Mission Planning: Reduces the time needed to screen landing zones and adapt to launch schedule shifts.

​STEM Accessibility: Translates complex orbital mechanics and topographic datasets into an intuitive visual interface for students and the public.

​Tools, Languages & Software Used:

​Frontend & 3D Visualization: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js / WebGL, Chart.js

​Backend & Data Processing: Python, NumPy, SciPy, Astropy (for coordinate transformations and horizon ray-casting)
